extraction.name: ACL OCL
extraction.description: A scholarly corpus derived from the ACL Anthology to assist Open scientific research in the Computational Linguistics domain. It contributes metadata, PDF files, citation graphs, structured full texts, figures, and links to Semantic Scholar.
extraction.creator: Shaurya Rohatgi, Yanxia Qin, Benjamin Aw, Niranjana Unnithan, Min-Yen Kan
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Crawled PDF files and metadata from the ACL Anthology website, removed PDFs longer than 50 pages, and used Semantic Scholar's API to fetch additional information.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Full-text extraction failed mostly for papers between the years 2000 to 2015. Common issues include missing section names, merged paragraphs, mixing of footnotes with texts, and misidentifying texts as table captions.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: ACL Anthology website and Semantic Scholar Academic Graph (S2AG)
extraction.rai:dataImputationProtocol: Incorrect metadata extracted from PDFs was replaced with metadata from the ACL Anthology.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: PDF files longer than 50 pages were removed. Figures and tables were extracted from PDF files using PDFFigures and stored separately. Language and topic fields were automatically detected and added.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: PDF files were passed through GROBID for full-text extraction into S2ORC-JSON format, which includes metadata, authors, and body text with citations, references, and sections.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Silver-labeled topic information was integrated by training a pre-trained language model (PLM) based topic classification method on a subset of 2,545 scientific papers with ground truth topic labels crawled from online held CL conferences.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Language detection toolkit (langdetect), GROBID, PDFFigures, and PLM-based topic classification models (SciBERT, SPECTER).
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset undergoes annual updates to download and process new papers added to the ACL Anthology. The authors plan to update OCL by year to keep it alive.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Accelerates scientific progress and promotes reproducibility in research by providing researchers with accessible and standardized data resources.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: English is the dominant language, and numerous low-resource languages remain underrepresented. There is also a bias in the distribution of top-cited papers towards dominant topics like Machine Translation.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: It is a small-scale collection focusing only on peer-reviewed and open-access CL papers from the ACL Anthology, not a comprehensive corpus. It lacks annotations for specific tasks that require labels. Full-text extraction quality is limited by GROBID's capabilities, struggling with tables, figures, and in-line equations.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Topic trend analysis, document-level terminology detection, coreference resolution, pre-training scientific large language models, fine-tuning general LLMs, building scientific assistants, summarization, related work generation, and multimodal research tasks.

name.evidence: We present the ACL OCL (or OCL for short), an enriched and contemporary scholarly corpus...

description.evidence: We present ACL OCL, a scholarly corpus derived from the ACL Anthology to assist Open scientific research in the Computational Linguistics domain. Integrating and enhancing the previous versions of the ACL Anthology, the ACL OCL contributes metadata, PDF files, citation graphs and additional structured full texts with sections, figures, and links to a large knowledge resource (Semantic Scholar).

inLanguage.evidence: English is the most dominant language processed in the ACL OCL. However, it is noteworthy that languages such as Latin and Gujarati are also present.

isLiveDataset.evidence: The dataset undergoes annual updates, during which we download and process papers recently added to the ACL Anthology.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: We start by crawling the PDF files and metadata from the source ACL Anthology... We remove PDF files longer than 50 pages... We enhance this data using Semantic Scholar’s API to fetch additional information about OCL papers.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: From the ACL Anthology, we design crawlers to fetch all the PDF documents and metadata from its website... We use its Graph API8 to connect an OCL document to its corresponding document in S2AG.

rai:dataCollectionMissingData.evidence: We observe that our full-text extraction fail mostly for papers between the years 2000 to 2015... For general text extraction, some common issues include missing section names, merged paragraphs, the mixing of footnotes with texts, and misidentifying texts as table captions.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: From the ACL Anthology, we design crawlers to fetch all the PDF documents and metadata from its website... We link the OCL corpus with knowledge graphs to enrich OCL with extemal information... We choose the recently released Semantic Scholar Academic Graph (S2AG, Kinney et al., 2023)

rai:dataCollectionTimeframe.evidence: The OCL corpus includes 73,285 papers hosted by the ACL Anthology published from 1952 to September 2022.

rai:dataImputationProtocol.evidence: Incorrect metadata such as author names exceeding three tokens, is a common issue. In response, the OCL uses the metadata from ACL Anthology.

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: We remove PDF files longer than 50 pages, which are mostly conference volume introductions or handbooks... we extract figures and tables from PDF files using PDFFigures... We add automatically detected fields such as language and topic to enable further analysis.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: We then pass the PDF files through the full-text extraction process... we use GROBID for the full-text extraction from PDF files. We take the S2ORC-JSON format used by Lo et al. (2020) and Wang et al. (2020) for our full-text schema

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: We first train a pre-trained language model (PLM) based topic classification method on a subset of 2,545 scientific papers with ground truth topic labels. We then extrapolate and integrate the model predictions as silver-labeled topic information in the OCL.

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: we utilize a public language detection toolkit (Shuyo, 2010)... we use GROBID for the full-text extraction... we extract figures and tables from PDF files using PDFFigures... we utilize a PLM-based classification framework for our task... namely SciBERT (Maheshwari et al., 2021) and SPECTER

rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan.evidence: The dataset undergoes annual updates, during which we download and process papers recently added to the ACL Anthology... We plan to update OCL by year to keep it alive.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: Building scholarly corpora for open research accelerates scientific progress and promotes reproducibility in research by providing researchers with accessible and standardized data resources.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: English is the most dominant language processed in the ACL OCL... numerous languages remain underrepresented... mainly because of the bias in the distribution of top-cited papers towards dominant topics (e.g., MT).

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: The OCL corpus is a small-scale collection of documents specifically focusing on peer-reviewed and open-access CL papers. As a result, it is not a comprehensive corpus like S2ORC... The OCL corpus is an unlabeled resource, lacking annotations for specific tasks that require labels... As with other toolkits, GROBID also struggles with the extraction of tables and figures, especially in-line equations.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: We spotlight how ACL OCL applies to observe trends in computational linguistics... OCL aids tasks that demand complete textual content from scientific papers, such as document-level terminology detection, coreference resolution, pre-training scientific large language models... The full texts and figures provision multimodal research tasks such as summarization
